newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - supply takes center stage.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - supply takes center stage.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bond prices were unchanged to up 1/8 in late morning trade as dealers drew their sights on a variety of offerings hitting the primary market.
While the muni market is lagging the U.S. Treasury market, it is still up, one trader said.
Almost half of the $1.5 billion of deals slated for sale on Tuesday have come to market and are getting a good reception, helped in part by the U.S. Treasury market.
"The deals are going well," said the trader.

So far Tuesday, a number of issues have hit the market, including the $385 million Local Government Assistance Corporation, which had been day-to-day this week. The New York issue was priced with a top yield of 5.675 percent in 2019 through a syndicate headed by Bear Stearns & Co.
Other New york issues of size included a Monroe County, N.Y., $148 million general obligation issue priced with a top yield of 5.45 percent in 2017.

Lehman Brothers won a $40 million Orlando Utilities Commission electric revenue bond offering with a true interest cost of 5.303 percent, while Prudential Securities took the $60 million portion with a TIC of 4.39 percent.,

On the West Coast, Smith Barney said it won $118 million of Airports Commission of the city and county of San Francisco, Calif., International Airport second series revenue bonds, issue 13B and 14, AMT, with a true interest cost (TIC) of 5.809 percent.

JP Morgan Securities said it won $131 million of Airports Commission of the city and county of San FRancisco, Calif., International Airport second series revenue bonds, issue 13A, taxable, with a true interest cost (TIC) of 7.2604 percent.
The muni offerings were sold into a strong U.S Treasury market, where at 1130 EST the benchmark 30-year bond was up about 13/32 to yield 6.44 percent.
Ahead of Tuesday's deal deluge, municipal bond prices ended flat to 1/4 softer on Monday.

Scheduled competitive and negotiated municipal bond sales are expected to total $1.55 billion in 55 offerings for Tuesday. Competitive sales total $527 million in 35 offerings. Negotiated sales total $1.02 billion in 20 offerings.
In debt futures, the December municipal contract was up 7/32 at 117 5/32. The December T-bond contract was up 12/32 at 115 7/32. The MOB spread was 57 ticks.
